statement: Voyage to the Blue Planet was a 2024 concert tour by the American rock band Weezer.
The band first teased a 30th anniversary tour for their self-titled debut studio album in December 2023.
Weezer's self-titled debut studio album is commonly known as the Blue Album.
The band officially announced the tour in March 2024.
The tour took place in North America.
The tour consisted of 24 shows.
22 of the tour's shows were in the United States.
Two of the tour's shows were in Canada.
The tour was produced by Live Nation.
The tour was sponsored by Citigroup.
The show featured The Flaming Lips as an opening act.
The show featured Dinosaur Jr. as an opening act.
The show had an outer space aesthetic.
The show's plot concerned the band traveling to the dying Blue Planet.
The band saved the Blue Planet by playing the entire discography of the Blue Album as part of the show's plot.
Songs from other albums were also played during the tour.
These other albums included Pinkerton, the Green Album, and the Red Album.
The tour received generally positive reviews from critics.
Critics praised the show's camp aesthetic.
Critics praised the performance from the band.
A concert film showcasing the band's performance in Boston was released.
In a December 2023 interview, Steve Weintraub of Collider asked the members of Weezer about plans to commemorate the 30th anniversary of their debut album Weezer.
Weezer's debut album was first released in May 1994.
Rivers Cuomo is the band's lead vocalist.
Rivers Cuomo said that there had not been a big commemoration for the album's 20th anniversary.
Rivers Cuomo said the band intended to celebrate the 30th anniversary with 'a really amazing deluxe package with a bunch of additional material'.
Rivers Cuomo said the band intended to celebrate the 30th anniversary with 'some kind of epic tour'.
Cuomo added that their touring schedule was free after June 2024.
Cuomo hinted that an anniversary tour may happen in the months following June 2024.
In February 2024, Cuomo made a post on his Facebook account.
The post included a link to 'BlueVoyage2024.com'.
The post included the caption 'Are you prepared for the voyage?'.
The website 'BlueVoyage2024.com' asked visitors to sign up for an email mailing list.
The website 'BlueVoyage2024.com' said, 'The voyage takes flight on March 11, 2024'.
Several news outlets stated that the 'Blue Voyage' could be a reference to an anniversary tour for the Blue Album.
On March 11, Live Nation Entertainment announced that presale tickets for the tour would be available to members of the band's mailing list starting on March 13.
The tour was officially called the 'Voyage to the Blue Planet'.
The tour was scheduled to begin in Saint Paul, Minnesota, on September 4.
The tour was scheduled to run for 22 shows.
The tour was scheduled to conclude in Inglewood, California, on October 11.
The tour would be produced by Live Nation.
The tour would be sponsored by Citigroup.
Presale tickets would also be available to Citigroup card holders.
General admission tickets would open on March 15.
General admission tickets would be available through Live Nation's sister company Ticketmaster.
Dinosaur Jr. would serve as an opening act for the tour.
The Flaming Lips would serve as an opening act for the tour.
Separate from the tour, Weezer planned to perform an anniversary concert on March 15.
The anniversary concert was planned to be held at the Lodge Room in Los Angeles.
Dogstar was planned to serve as Weezer's supporting act for the anniversary concert.
In June 2024, Weezer added another show in Palm Desert, California, on October 12.
This added show would serve as the tour's final show.
A second show was scheduled for September 15 in Washington, D.C.
Following the tour's conclusion, Weezer said that the tour had been their 'best tour ever'.
The band later played the setlist during the Bumbershoot music festival in Seattle.
This performance occurred on August 30, 2025.
The show began with a breaking news alert announcing a voyage into outer space.
The show then segued into a countdown.
At the end of the countdown, the band appeared on stage.
The band was clad in astronaut gear.
A spacecraft lifted up, leaving behind white clouds.
Cuomo told the audience that they were embarking on a 'very dangerous mission'.
Cuomo told the audience they were traveling 30 light years away to save the Blue Planet.
Over the course of the show, the band interacts with an alien known as Bokkus.
Bokkus serves as the main antagonist for the band in the show.
Throughout the first part of the show, the band played songs from several different albums.
'Hash Pipe' is from the Green Album.
'Pork and Beans' is from the Red Album.
During several of the songs, visual motifs appeared on a large screen behind the band.
Red planets appeared during the Red Album song 'Troublemaker'.
Palm trees appeared during their performance of 'Beverly Hills'.
'Troublemaker' is a Red Album song.
During 'Perfect Situation', the screen on stage showed the band's spacecraft engaged in a fight with Bokkus.
Bokkus damages the ship during the fight shown on screen.
Following this, the band is interrupted by a CGI character on the screen.
The CGI character informed the band that they were stranded in the 'Pinkerton Asteroid Belt'.
This prompted the band to play several songs from their album Pinkerton.
'Why Bother?' is a song from the album Pinkerton.
About halfway through the show, the band landed on the Blue Planet.
The Blue Planet was depicted as a dull and dying planet in the show.
Cuomo planted a flag bearing the band's logo.
Cuomo announced, 'One small step for Weezer, one giant leap for Weezer-kind'.
Cuomo stated that the way to save the planet was to sing the songs from the Blue Album.
At that point, the band began to play 'My Name Is Jonas'.
During this part of the concert, Bokkus battled with Cuomo.
Aliens named Weezeroids appeared on the screen.
The Weezeroids resembled Cuomo.
Cuomo told the audience that he was an alien.
Cuomo told the audience that the audience themselves were aliens.
Cuomo's announcement was followed by a playing of 'Undone – The Sweater Song'.
Weezer ended the concert with a playing of 'Only in Dreams'.
During the song's crescendo, confetti cannons erupted.
The band thanked the audience before departing the stage.
The band thanked their opening bands before departing the stage.
The band thanked their crew before departing the stage.
The show lasted about an hour and a half.
The tour received mostly positive reviews from critics.
Evan Minsker is from Rolling Stone.
Evan Minsker reviewed the premier show in Saint Paul.
Evan Minsker said that the band has 'reached new heights as an arena band'.
Evan Minsker particularly praised the camp approach employed by the band.
Evan Minsker said that the show felt like a combination of an Iron Maiden concert and Disneyland's Star Tours attraction.
Chris Stevens is from Boston.com.
Chris Stevens reviewed the Boston show.
Chris Stevens said he agreed with The Flaming Lips' lead vocalist Wayne Coyne in calling the show 'effing mind blowing'.
Wayne Coyne is The Flaming Lips' lead vocalist.
Chris Stevens stated that the show was 'all camp, all fun'.
Aiden J. Bowers is from The Harvard Crimson.
Aiden J. Bowers reviewed the same performance.
Aiden J. Bowers praised the band's performance.
Aiden J. Bowers said the band was 'at their best'.
Aiden J. Bowers said that the last moments of the show 'brought out some of Weezer's best musical work'.
Audrey Gibbs is from The Tennessean.
Audrey Gibbs gave a positive review of the Nashville show.
Audrey Gibbs praised Cuomo's performance.
Ethan Shanfeld is from Variety.
Ethan Shanfeld gave an overall positive review of the tour.
Ethan Shanfeld criticized certain aspects of the tour.
Ethan Shanfeld's criticism included the aesthetics.
Ethan Shanfeld said that at one point the show resembled a performance by The Wiggles.
Ethan Shanfeld's criticism included song selection.
Ethan Shanfeld criticized the inclusion of a song from Pacific Daydream.
Ethan Shanfeld criticized the absence of any song from the White Album.
James Sullivan is from The Boston Globe.
James Sullivan gave a mixed review.
James Sullivan criticized the aesthetics.
James Sullivan said that by the time the band began its performance of songs from the Blue Album, 'the kitschy video-game backdrop had worn a little thin'.
